name: Waterloo
summary: Wellington's Anglo-allied army held the ridge of Mont-Saint-Jean through a long afternoon of French attacks: on Hougoumont, d'Erlon's great columns, Ney's cavalry and finally the Imperial Guard. From late afternoon Blücher's Prussians came up on Napoleon's right at Plancenoit, and in the evening the French army broke.

sources.label: Prussian Army of the Lower Rhine, June 1815 (Nafziger Collection 815FAG, after Plotho)

forces.name: Picton's Division
forces.summary: Peninsula veterans held behind the hedges on the allied left centre. When d'Erlon's corps came up the slope in the early afternoon, Kempt's and Pack's brigades met it with volleys and the bayonet before the Union Brigade charged through. Picton was killed leading the counter-attack.
notes: Pack's brigade had two Highland battalions, the 42nd and 92nd, where the list allows one Highland battalion in four, so it shows as a historical departure.
The 1/95th is the list's Rifle Battalion, taken as the Rifles upgrade on a Line battalion.
The named Kempt and Pack from the book can be added under Army command instead.
Major Heise commanded the division's artillery; it's shown as Rogers' and Braun's batteries.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Alten's Division
forces.summary: British, King's German Legion and Hanoverian brigades in the allied centre, just west of the Brussels road behind La Haye Sainte. They stood in square through Ney's great cavalry charges; Ompteda's KGL held the farm until it fell in the evening, and Ompteda was killed leading a counter-attack. Alten was wounded and Kielmansegge took over the division.
notes: Ompteda's brigade had two KGL Light battalions, where the list allows one in four, so it shows as a historical departure. Baring's 2nd Light garrisoned La Haye Sainte.
Alten is the book's named commander.
Kielmansegge's Feldjäger (two companies) are the list's Jäger Companies.
Lloyd's and Cleeves' batteries are the two the order of battle gives under Lt-Col Williamson after Alten's brigades.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces, except the book's named Lieutenant General Count Charles Alten, with his own rating.

forces.name: Cooke's Guards Division
forces.summary: Held the allied right. Its light companies, with others, defended the château of Hougoumont all day, while Maitland's brigade lay behind the ridge until it rose to meet the Guard's last attack in the evening.
notes: The division was two Guards brigades, with none of the British and Hanoverian brigades the list needs. The list allows one Guards Brigade, taken once two British or KGL brigades are, so these show as historical departures.
Support brigades like these can be at most half an army, and the list allows horse artillery by the cavalry taken, so Kuhlmann's KGL horse battery shows as a departure too.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Clinton's Division
forces.summary: Stood in reserve behind Hougoumont through the afternoon. In the evening Adam's brigade swung forward against the flank of the Imperial Guard's attack, and the 52nd's volleys helped break it.
notes: The 1/52nd, over a thousand strong, is Large, and the 1/71st Highlanders; the 2/95th is the list's Rifle Battalion and the two companies of the 3/95th its Rifle Company.

Adam's brigade had only three battalions, too few for the list's one-in-four Highland and Large upgrades, and Sympher's KGL horse battery is more horse artillery than a division with no cavalry is allowed; these show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Lambert's and Best's Brigades
forces.summary: Came up from Brussels to the allied left centre, and was sent forward to plug the line around La Haye Sainte in the late afternoon, suffering heavily.
notes: Cole, the 6th Division's commander, wasn't there; Lambert led his brigade, with Best's Hanoverians, which the order of battle lists alongside it. The 2/81st was left in Brussels.
Sinclair's battery is the one the order of battle lists after the division.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Perponcher's Division
forces.formation: 2nd Netherlands Division, I Corps (Prince of Orange)
forces.summary: Formed on the allied left centre. Bijlandt's brigade, worn down at Quatre Bras, stood in the path of d'Erlon's attack; Saxe-Weimar's Nassauers held the farms of Papelotte and La Haye on the far left all day.
notes: Bijlandt's brigade had lost heavily at Quatre Bras; Small upgrades are a fair way to show it.
The order of battle gives Goedecke as the 2nd Brigade's commander; Saxe-Weimar led it after Goedecke was hurt before the campaign opened.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Chassé's Division
forces.formation: 3rd Netherlands Division, I Corps (Prince of Orange)
forces.summary: In reserve on the far right until the evening, when Chassé brought it into the centre, where it helped turn back the last attack of the Imperial Guard.
notes: Both brigades had six battalions where the list allows five, and Detmers had four Militia battalions where it allows three, so these show as historical departures.
Chassé is the book's named commander.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces, except the book's named Lieutenant General David Hendrik, Baron Chassé, with his own rating.

forces.name: Kruse's Nassauers
forces.summary: Stood in the allied centre beside the Brussels road, behind La Haye Sainte, and fought to hold the line there as the farm fell.
notes: The Nassau contingent was one big regiment of three battalions, each nearly a thousand strong, so all three are Large.
On its own it has no Dutch/Belgian Infantry Brigade, which the list needs, so that shows as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: The Brunswick Corps
forces.summary: Stood in the centre-right through the great cavalry charges, then went forward to close the line beside Alten's division in the evening.
notes: The Duke of Brunswick had been killed at Quatre Bras, so Olfermann commanded at Waterloo.
The order of battle's Guard Battalion is the list's Leib Light Battalion.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: The Household and Union Brigades
forces.summary: Charged d'Erlon's broken columns in the early afternoon, scattering them and taking two eagles, then rode on into the French guns and were cut up by lancers and cuirassiers.
notes: Two heavy brigades on their own: the list needs British and Hanoverian infantry brigades, and its heavy cavalry comes with them, and the Household Brigade had three Household regiments where it allows two, and support brigades can be at most half an army, so these show as historical departures.
Uxbridge led the charge in person, as the army's cavalry commander.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Vandeleur's and Vivian's Light Cavalry
forces.summary: Guarded the allied left flank until the Prussians arrived, then moved to the centre in the evening and charged in the final general advance.
notes: Two light brigades on their own: the list needs British and Hanoverian infantry brigades, its light cavalry comes with them, and support brigades can be at most half an army, so these show as historical departures.
Gardiner's troop is one of the horse artillery troops attached to the cavalry.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Donzelot's Division
forces.summary: One of the four divisions of d'Erlon's corps that attacked the allied left centre in massed columns in the early afternoon, beside La Haye Sainte. Thrown back with the rest of the corps by Picton's infantry and the Union Brigade, it rallied and helped take the farm late in the day.
notes: The 13e Léger brought all three battalions, where the list allows one Light battalion in four across the army, so the third shows as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Marcognet's Division
forces.summary: Advancing on d'Erlon's right-centre, its columns crested the ridge into Pack's brigade and were caught by the Scots Greys of the Union Brigade; the 45e lost its eagle. What was left rallied and fought on into the evening.
notes: Every regiment fielded two battalions, so the division fits the list as it fought.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Quiot's Division
forces.summary: The left-hand division of d'Erlon's great attack, part of it against La Haye Sainte and the rest up the slope towards Kempt's brigade, before the Union Brigade drove it back.
notes: Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Durutte's Division
forces.summary: On d'Erlon's right, attacking towards Papelotte. It kept its order when the rest of the corps was broken, and fought on against the farms into the evening.
notes: Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Prince Jérôme's Division
forces.summary: Opened the battle against Hougoumont and spent the whole day trying to take it, drawing in far more men than the allied garrison.
notes: Prince Jérôme commanded, though Guilleminot, his chief of staff, did much of the work.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Foy's Division
forces.summary: Fed into the fighting around Hougoumont, then joined Bachelu's late infantry attack between the château and La Haye Sainte.
notes: The 4e Léger brought three battalions, one more Light battalion than the list's one in four allows, which shows as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Bachelu's Division
forces.summary: Stood in reserve behind Hougoumont until the evening, when it and Foy's division made a last infantry attack after the great cavalry charges had failed.
notes: Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Simmer's Division
forces.summary: Sent east with Lobau's corps to hold off the Prussians, it fought for Plancenoit through the late afternoon and evening.
notes: Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

commander.name: Gén. de Brigade Julienne de Bellair

forces.name: Jeanin's Division
forces.summary: Lobau's second division, small after detachments, holding the ground in front of Plancenoit against Bülow's corps.
notes: Tromelin's brigade had only the 107e's two battalions, fewer than the list's three for a brigade, and the 5e Léger's two battalions are one more Light battalion than one in four allows; both show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Wathier's Cuirassiers
forces.summary: Led Ney's great cavalry charges against the allied squares between Hougoumont and La Haye Sainte through the middle of the afternoon.
notes: A cavalry division on its own has no Infantry Brigade, which the list needs; its cavalry brigades are allowed by infantry brigades, and reserve cavalry can be at most half an army. So these show as historical departures. Play it alongside an infantry division, or agree it with your opponent.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Delort's Cuirassiers
forces.summary: Joined Milhaud's charges on the allied centre, riding round the squares again and again under the allied guns.
notes: A cavalry division on its own has no Infantry Brigade, which the list needs; its cavalry brigades are allowed by infantry brigades, and reserve cavalry can be at most half an army. So these show as historical departures. Play it alongside an infantry division, or agree it with your opponent.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: L'Héritier's Division
forces.summary: Kellermann's corps, sent in to join Milhaud's charges on the allied squares late in the afternoon.
notes: A cavalry division on its own has no Infantry Brigade, which the list needs; its cavalry brigades are allowed by infantry brigades, and reserve cavalry can be at most half an army. So these show as historical departures. Play it alongside an infantry division, or agree it with your opponent.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Roussel d'Hurbal's Division
forces.summary: The carabiniers and cuirassiers of Kellermann's second division, committed to the cavalry charges on the allied centre.
notes: A cavalry division on its own has no Infantry Brigade, which the list needs; its cavalry brigades are allowed by infantry brigades, and reserve cavalry can be at most half an army. So these show as historical departures. Play it alongside an infantry division, or agree it with your opponent.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Jacquinot's Light Cavalry
forces.summary: Guarded d'Erlon's right flank, and its lancers fell on the Union Brigade when it charged too far.
notes: A cavalry division on its own has no Infantry Brigade, which the list needs; its cavalry brigades are allowed by infantry brigades, and reserve cavalry can be at most half an army. So these show as historical departures. Play it alongside an infantry division, or agree it with your opponent.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: The Old Guard
forces.formation: 1st and 2nd Grenadiers and Chasseurs à Pied
forces.summary: The Emperor's last reserve. Battalions went to retake Plancenoit from the Prussians; at the end, the 1st and 2nd Grenadiers and Chasseurs formed the squares that covered the retreat.
notes: Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: The Middle Guard
forces.formation: 3rd and 4th Grenadiers and Chasseurs à Pied
forces.summary: Made the last French attack of the day up the slope west of La Haye Sainte, and was broken by Maitland's Guards and Adam's brigade.
notes: Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: The Young Guard
forces.summary: Sent to hold Plancenoit against Bülow's Prussians, it fought in the village through the evening until driven out.
notes: Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: The Guard Cavalry
forces.formation: Guyot's heavy and Lefebvre-Desnouettes' light divisions
forces.summary: Followed Milhaud and Kellermann into the great charges on the allied squares in the late afternoon.
notes: The Guard cavalry rode without the three Guard infantry brigades the list asks for first, and the light division had two Lancer regiments where the list allows one; these show as historical departures.
The Chasseurs à Cheval, over 1,200 strong, are Large.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Bülow's IV Corps
forces.formation: IV Corps, Army of the Lower Rhine
forces.summary: The first Prussian corps onto the field, untouched at Ligny. Losthin's and Hiller's brigades came out of the Bois de Paris onto the French right in the late afternoon, and with Hake's and Ryssel's behind them fought Lobau's corps and the Young Guard for Plancenoit until it fell in the evening.
notes: A Prussian brigade was the size of another army's division, so the whole corps is here. Take the brigades you want; each is a force in itself.
Each regiment's three battalions are the list's two Musketeer and one Fusilier battalions, or three Landwehr. The order of battle doesn't number the brigades' foot batteries.

The corps cavalry, under Prince Wilhelm of Prussia, follows Nafziger's order of battle (after Plotho). The list takes line or Landwehr cavalry brigades but not both, so a corps with both shows it as a historical departure.
Sydow's brigade had seven Landwehr cavalry regiments, more than one of the list's brigades holds, so it is split in two here.

Nafziger gives each corps three 12-pdr batteries, a howitzer battery and more 6-pdr foot and horse batteries than its brigades had; the list's reserve takes one heavy, one foot and one horse battery, so only those are here. Which horse batteries rode with the cavalry brigades is our reading.
Bülow commands as the optional Corps Commander (Albion Triumphant p. his brigade commanders at 8, the list's lowest.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Zieten's I Corps
forces.formation: I Corps, Army of the Lower Rhine
forces.summary: Marched across from Wavre to join Wellington's left. Steinmetz's brigade led it onto the field near Papelotte in the evening, and pushed into the French right as their line broke.
notes: The order of battle gives Pirch II's brigade four regiments, the 16th Infantry among them, where the list's brigade has at most two Line regiments and three in all, so these show as historical departures.
At Waterloo only Steinmetz's brigade, at the head of the column, was fully engaged; the rest of the corps was still coming up.
A Prussian brigade was the size of another army's division, so the whole corps is here. Take the brigades you want; each is a force in itself.
Each regiment's three battalions are the list's two Musketeer and one Fusilier battalions, or three Landwehr. The order of battle doesn't number the brigades' foot batteries.

The corps cavalry, under Röder, follows Nafziger's order of battle (after Plotho). The list takes line or Landwehr cavalry brigades but not both, so a corps with both shows it as a historical departure.
Lützow's brigade mixed line and Landwehr cavalry, which the list's brigades don't, so its two Landwehr regiments and the Westphalian are a brigade of their own here.

Nafziger gives each corps three 12-pdr batteries, a howitzer battery and more 6-pdr foot and horse batteries than its brigades had; the list's reserve takes one heavy, one foot and one horse battery, so only those are here. Which horse batteries rode with the cavalry brigades is our reading.
Zieten is the book's named commander.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces, except the book's named General Hans Ernst Karl, Graf von Zieten, with his own rating.
